name: iShareBlog
author: fareeddaar

sections.description:
iShareBlog helps readers share your posts, and gives them something good to say when they do.

  • Share buttons for X, Bluesky, Threads, Mastodon, Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, Reddit, Pinterest, email and copy link, plus a “Share” button that opens the phone’s own share menu. They are added before and/or after posts automatically, or placed with the “Share Buttons” block or the [ishareblog] shortcode. The default style is outlined and icon-only, and picks up your theme’s primary color automatically.
  • Floating and mobile share bar. An optional bar on the side of the screen on desktop, and along the bottom on phones. It appears once readers scroll, matches your site’s background, and steps aside while the buttons in the post are in view.
  • Per-post control. Hide the buttons on any post with one checkbox in the editor.
  • Prefilled summaries. Each button opens with a short summary of the post already written: X, Bluesky, Threads, Mastodon, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram and email are prefilled (shortened to fit each network’s limit), and Facebook copies the summary so the reader can paste it.
  • Summarize with ChatGPT. A button that opens ChatGPT with a prompt asking for an overview and the key takeaways of the post. Claude and Perplexity versions are also available.
  • Click-to-share quotes. Add the “Shareable Quote” block, or use [ishareblog_quote cite="Author"]Your quote[/ishareblog_quote] in the classic editor. Readers can also highlight any text in a post and share it from a small popup.
  • Social posts. A “Social Posts” box in the post editor drafts a post for X, LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram. These drafts are also the summaries used by the share buttons. On WordPress 7.0 and later it can write them with the WordPress AI Client, using whichever AI provider you set up in Settings → Connectors; otherwise it builds them from the title, excerpt and tags.
  • Share analytics. Total shares, shares per day, top networks, top posts and where shares come from (buttons, floating bar, quotes, highlighted text), plus a “Shares” column in your posts list.

No external scripts, tracking pixels or third-party requests are added to your pages.

External services

AI social posts. The plugin does not contact any AI service directly. If a site administrator turns on “Use AI”, it sends a prompt through the WordPress AI Client to the AI provider the site owner configured in Settings → Connectors; that provider’s terms and privacy policy apply. This happens when a user who can publish the post clicks “Generate social posts” (limited per user per day), and once, in the background, when a post is first published. Contributors only get template drafts. Long posts are shortened to 20,000 characters before sending. The post’s title, URL, tags and content, plus the “brand voice” text from the settings, are sent.

The share and “Summarize with” buttons are plain links. Nothing is sent to these services unless a reader clicks a button, and then the reader’s browser opens the service directly with the post’s URL, title and summary:
X (https://x.com/en/tos, https://x.com/en/privacy), Bluesky (https://bsky.social/about/support/tos, https://bsky.social/about/support/privacy-policy), Threads (https://help.instagram.com/769983657850450, https://help.instagram.com/515230437301944), Mastodon (the reader’s own server, which they choose; its terms and privacy policy apply), Facebook (https://www.facebook.com/terms.php, https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/), LinkedIn (https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement, https://www.linkedin.com/legal/privacy-policy), WhatsApp (https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/terms-of-service, https://www.whatsapp.com/legal/privacy-policy), Telegram (https://telegram.org/tos, https://telegram.org/privacy), Reddit (https://redditinc.com/policies/user-agreement, https://www.reddit.com/policies/privacy-policy), Pinterest (https://policy.pinterest.com/terms-of-service, https://policy.pinterest.com/privacy-policy), ChatGPT (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/, https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy/), Claude (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms, https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy), Perplexity (https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/terms-of-service, https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/legal/privacy-policy).
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin through Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, or install it from the plugin directory, then activate it.
  2. Go to iShareBlog → Settings to choose networks, style and placement.
  3. Optional (WordPress 7.0+): set up an AI provider in Settings → Connectors, then turn on “Use AI” in iShareBlog → Settings for AI-written summaries and social posts.
sections.faq:
How do I place the buttons manually?

Add the “Share Buttons” block where you want them; it replaces the automatic buttons on that post, and can use its own networks and heading. Or set Position to “Don’t insert automatically” and use [ishareblog], for example [ishareblog networks="x,bluesky,copy" heading="Spread the word"].

How do I hide the buttons on one post?

Tick “Hide share buttons on this post” in the “Share buttons” panel of the post editor’s sidebar. It also turns off the floating bar and highlight-to-share for that post.

How does the Mastodon button work?

Mastodon has no single share page, so the first time a reader clicks it they are asked for their server (for example mastodon.social). The browser remembers it for next time.

Why don’t I see the “Share” button?

It opens the device’s own share menu, which most phones and some desktop browsers have. Where the browser has no share menu, the button is hidden.

How do I add a shareable quote?

Use the “Shareable Quote” block, or [ishareblog_quote tweet="Optional custom share text" cite="Author"]Quote text[/ishareblog_quote].

Can I change the share text?

Yes. Edit the drafts in the post’s “Social Posts” box and update the post. X, Bluesky, Threads and Mastodon use the X draft, LinkedIn and email use the LinkedIn draft, and the other networks use the Facebook draft.

Which AI provider does it use?

Whichever one you set up for your site in Settings → Connectors (WordPress 7.0 or later). The plugin uses the WordPress AI Client and does not store any API keys itself.

My site is behind Cloudflare or another proxy. Does tracking still work?

Yes, but every visitor will appear to come from the proxy’s IP, so the per-visitor limits are shared. Pass the real visitor IP with a filter, using the header your proxy sets, for example:
add_filter( ‘ishareblog_client_ip’, function ( $ip ) { return isset( $_SERVER[‘HTTP_CF_CONNECTING_IP’] ) ? sanitize_text_field( wp_unslash( $_SERVER[‘HTTP_CF_CONNECTING_IP’] ) ) : $ip; } );
Only do this when your server is reachable only through the proxy.

Does it store personal data?

No. Analytics store only the post, the network, where the click came from (button, quote or highlighted text) and the time. To ignore repeated clicks, the visitor’s IP address is hashed with a site secret into temporary keys that expire within an hour; the IP itself is never stored.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • New: floating share bar for wide screens and a bottom share bar for phones.
  • New: “Share Buttons” block, with its own networks and heading.
  • New: Bluesky, Threads and Mastodon buttons, also available in the highlight-to-share popup (Bluesky and Threads).
  • New: “Share” button that opens the device’s share menu.
  • New: hide the share buttons on individual posts.
  • Analytics now shows shares from the floating bar separately.

1.0.2

  • AI social posts now use the WordPress AI Client (WordPress 7.0+) and the provider configured in Settings → Connectors. The plugin no longer calls the Anthropic API directly or stores an API key.
  • Fixed a “translation loading was triggered too early” notice.

1.0.1

  • The post body is no longer wrapped in an extra element, so theme spacing between paragraphs, lists and quotes is kept.

1.0.0

  • First release.
